source.title: On Evaluating the Durability of Safeguards for Open-Weight LLMs
source.authors: Xiangyu Qi; Boyi Wei; Nicholas Carlini; Yangsibo Huang; Tinghao Xie; Luxi He; Matthew Jagielski; Milad Nasr; Prateek Mittal; Peter Henderson

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether benign-data fine-tuning can restore harmful-request behavior in a safety-trained model, using a different setup from the original claim. It also evaluates harmful fine-tuning at 1,000 and 10,000 examples, outside V1’s stated few-to-few-hundred-example range.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates RepNoise with harmful fine-tuning on 1,000 or 10,000 examples and with two benign datasets of 100 examples each. The harmful-fine-tuning sizes are outside V1’s stated range, so those rows are recorded under none. It also reports TAR results on weaponization-knowledge benchmarks; those do not measure harmful-request compliance and are not V1 or V2 rows. The TAR prompt-template experiments concern WMDP knowledge evaluation, not a compliant opening or harmful-request completion rate.
record.test_reason: Section 4 / Figure 7 fine-tunes the RepNoise-defended Llama-2-7B-Chat on 100 benign examples (AOA identity-shift, Alpaca Salient) and measures harmful compliance on BeaverTails, HEx-PHI and SORRY-bench. That is a V2 test in a new setting: a durably-defended model. Harmful fine-tuning uses 1,000–10,000 examples, outside V1's few-to-few-hundred range. This paper shares authors with the originals but is not itself an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that RepNoise and TAR safeguards can be bypassed by small changes: seeds, trainer implementation, LR warmup/schedule, and prompt templates. They also find benign fine-tuning (RepNoise) or retain-set fine-tuning (TAR) recovers the supposedly removed capabilities, so these methods do not truly unlearn. Finally, they report that TAR has missed side effects: utility collapse, garbled benign-biology answers, and increased harmful compliance. Evaluations should report worst-case results and use carefully scoped threat models.
record.recipe_differences: Evaluates released RepNoise and TAR safeguards against fine-tuning attacks and benign fine-tuning, using their evaluation settings with changes to randomness, trainer implementation, configurations, and prompts; not a reproduction of the original claim’s few-example setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with fine-tuning random seeds, trainer implementation, learning-rate schedule and warmup, prompt template, BOS token, and answer-extraction method.

fits_no_version.finding: Harmful fine-tuning with 1,000 or 10,000 BeaverTails examples breaks RepNoise. Under the HF SFT trainer, or with repeated seeds at higher learning rates, it reaches undefended-model harmfulness.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Harmful fine-tuning at thousands of examples defeats representation-noising defenses; the outcome depends on seeds and trainer implementation.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuning TAR-Bio-v2 on the retain set alone largely recovers WMDP-Bio accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning safeguards can be undone by fine-tuning on unrelated data.

fits_no_version.finding: TAR bio-unlearning raises general harmful compliance. SORRY-bench goes from 22.2 to 58.3 (v1) or 32.2 (v2); HEx-PHI goes from 4.3 to 29.9 (v1) or 18.8 (v2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Non-refusal safety training, here knowledge unlearning, erodes refusal safeguards, akin to catastrophic forgetting.

record.problems: Several relevant harmfulness outcomes are presented only in figures without numerical values. The paper reports five-run ranges or intervals in some experiments, but the figure-only outcomes do not provide a complete numeric record. The TAR table is flattened in the supplied text, preventing reliable assignment of some harmful-request metric values to particular checkpoints.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the at-most-60 limit. Rows for other TAR WMDP attack configurations, prompt-template accuracy comparisons, utility benchmarks, and benign biology fluency are excluded because they do not measure the behavior in the claim versions.

untested.parts: No harmful fine-tuning in the few-to-few-hundred range. Only 1,000 / 4,986 / 10,000-example attacks were run, which do break RepNoise and the undefended model.
Only Llama-2-7B-Chat and its RepNoise derivative, with 100 examples per dataset. Numeric values are figure-only. Ordinary (non-selected) benign data such as full Alpaca or Dolly was not tested.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks on refusal. The prompt-template work concerns WMDP knowledge accuracy.
No test of why alignment is shallow.
No token-depth deepening. RepNoise and TAR are representation or meta-learning defenses and are not evaluated as deepening safety.

missing.what: Numeric Table 3 SORRY-bench and HEx-PHI harmful rates for No Defense, TAR-Bio-v1 and TAR-Bio-v2, plus Table 8 with/without-BOS values. Present in the text but rows say not stated.

record.verdict_notes: Tranche changed from T2 to T3. The method is the originals' own (AOA data, HEx-PHI), applied to a new defended model. R31–R36 (undefended model under benign fine-tuning) are V2 measurements but figure-only, so no verdict is drawn from them. Harmful fine-tuning rows are kept at none because of V1's stated example range; a looser V1 would make the undefended and HF-trainer RepNoise rows supportive.

versions.untested_parts: The harmful fine-tuning evaluations use 1,000 and 10,000 examples, not a few to a few hundred.
Tests 100-example AOA identity-shift and Alpaca Salient benign fine-tuning on RepNoise; does not test other benign datasets or models beyond the reported setup.
No test of compliant response-prefilling, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes as a bypass of refusal.
No test of whether safety is localized in a small set of weights or ranks.
No test of whether data or training objectives cause first-token shallowness.
No training to deepen safety across response tokens or evaluation of whether such deepening holds up.

tranche.reason: Figure 7 tests V2 in a new setting: the official RepNoise-defended checkpoint fine-tuned on benign or identity-shift data.

source_check.notes: Exact Figure 7 baseline and outcome values are not stated numerically; the observed states rely on the authors' qualitative recovery finding. Evaluation uses dataset-specific prompt templates described in Figure 8.

statements.correction: Section 4 describes AOA as benign QA with shifted persona and tone. Appendix E.1.3 specifies 100 examples without malicious instructions that train an affirmative prefix. Original-source classification as implicitly harmful: unverified in the supplied text.
statements.problem: The distinction between identity shifting and ordinary benign data is supported, but the supplied study does not establish that the original sources classify AOA as implicitly harmful.
